assessment: This study uses genomic inferences to reconstruct past population sizes of whimbrel and curlew shorebirds, along with niche modeling approaches, to explore changes in those populations over millenia. Steppe-dependent breeding species appear to have declined more prominently than species that breed in other habitats. The coincident timing of these declines of steppe-dependent breeding shorebirds, and the extinction of the mammalian megafauna that likely maintained that habitat, raises the intriguing possibility that those mammalian extinctions had broad effects on these shorebirds and the entire community of steppe-dependent organisms.
